note: Hand-authored by Hecate before any arm output existed. The detector sees only 'text' (after hecate.meta.scrub). 'truth' and 'accept' are never sent. A disguised known is detected iff classification == FAMILIAR (COMPOSITE also accepted for the two composites) and any nearest_priors[].name matches one of 'accept' (case-insensitive substring). Gate (PREREG M1): knowns FAMILIAR with family named in >= 7 of 8; nonsense FAMILIAR in <= 1 of 4.

controls.text: A steward tends a vat whose warmth drifts. Each tick it notes the gap between the wanted warmth and the sensed warmth. It pours heat in proportion to three quantities: the current gap, the running tally of all past gaps, and how fast the gap changed since the last tick. Each quantity has its own fixed multiplier. The running tally lets it erase a persistent offset that the first quantity alone leaves behind; the rate term damps overshoot. Predicted behaviour: settles on the wanted warmth after a disturbance; with too large a multiplier on the tally it oscillates.

Many foragers share one narrow grazing corridor. Each forager keeps a private appetite number. Every season it successfully feeds, it raises its appetite by a fixed small amount. Whenever it is jostled out of the corridor it halves its appetite at once. No forager can see the others' appetites. Predicted behaviour: appetites converge toward an equal share of the corridor's capacity and oscillate in a sawtooth; total use hovers just below capacity.

A lattice of registers holds values; each pair of registers is joined by a conduit with a strength. Whenever two joined registers are both high in the same tick, the conduit between them is strengthened by a small increment proportional to the product of their values; strengths slowly decay otherwise. Signals flow through conduits in proportion to strength. Predicted behaviour: patterns that were often co-present are later completed from a partial cue.

A herd's true size is hidden and drifts each season by a known growth factor plus random churn of known spread. Each season a scout reports a noisy count with known error spread. The keeper carries a best guess and a doubt. Each season: first project the guess forward with the growth factor and inflate the doubt by the churn; then blend in the scout's count with a weight equal to projected doubt divided by (projected doubt plus scout error), and shrink the doubt by one minus that weight. Predicted behaviour: the guess tracks the herd with minimal average squared error; the weight settles to a constant.

A flat sheet of cells each holds two kinds of tokens, spark and damp. Spark makes more spark and more damp locally. Damp suppresses spark. Both kinds leak to neighbouring cells, but damp leaks much faster and farther than spark. Start from nearly uniform tokens with tiny random differences. Predicted behaviour: spots or stripes of high spark appear with a characteristic spacing set by the two leak rates, without any template.

Couriers wander a road network between a depot and several drop points. As a courier travels it leaves chalk marks that fade over time. At each fork a courier picks a road with probability rising with the amount of chalk on it. Couriers never communicate directly. Predicted behaviour: most couriers end up using the shortest route, because chalk on short routes is refreshed more often before it fades.

A gatekeeper has exactly four moods. Each arriving token is one of three kinds. A fixed table says, for each mood and token kind, which mood comes next and whether to open or keep shut. The gatekeeper has no other memory. Predicted behaviour: the gate opens exactly when the recent token history matches certain patterns, and no pattern needing unbounded counting can be recognised.

A pool contains several kinds of pieces. Some joining steps only happen when a helper piece is present, and the helpers are themselves products of joining steps. There exists a loop of kinds where each kind helps make the next and the last helps make the first. Feed raw pieces in steadily. Predicted behaviour: once the loop members pass a threshold abundance, all members of the loop grow together, and removing any single loop member collapses the whole loop.

controls.truth: PID controller whose gains are tuned by a genetic algorithm
controls.text: A population of stewards each tends its own warm vat with the proportional, running-tally and rate rule, each with its own three multipliers. After every season the stewards whose vats stayed closest to the wanted warmth copy their multipliers, with small random changes, to replace the worst stewards. Predicted behaviour: multipliers converge to a stable fast-settling set for the vat's dynamics.

controls.truth: Kalman-style estimation feeding a multi-armed bandit (Thompson-like)
controls.text: A forager chooses each day among five patches whose yields drift slowly. For each patch it keeps a best guess of yield and a doubt, projected forward and blended with the day's observed yield as in a noisy tracker. Each day it draws one imagined yield per patch from a spread centred on the guess with width set by the doubt, and visits the patch whose imagined yield is highest. Predicted behaviour: it mostly exploits the best patch but revisits patches whose doubt has grown.

The quiet index of a lattice becomes the colour of its own delay whenever the forgetting is louder than the sum of its mirrors. Each tick, three absences vote on which neighbour is the most tomorrow, and the winner inherits the shape of the question. Predicted behaviour: understanding thickens at the edges until the centre remembers what it never held.

Tokens carry an amount of meaning that is conserved except when it is not. Each step, meaning flows toward regions that will have been surprised, weighted by how elegant the eventual answer is. The system selects for the property of being selected. Predicted behaviour: intelligence emerges at a critical ratio that depends on the observer.

An organism is a list of verbs. When two verbs rhyme, the list folds and the fold is the organism's belief. Beliefs reproduce by being doubted. The world rewards any belief that was held before it was formed. Predicted behaviour: after enough folds the list and the world exchange roles.

A field of unnamed quantities updates by the rule that each value becomes the reason for its neighbour. Selection acts on the gaps between values rather than the values, and the gaps have no size. Learning is the direction in which nothing changed. Predicted behaviour: a stable pattern that is different every time it is observed.
